passage:
Tuesday
Mohit got 4 out of 20 in his spelling test. I saw it in his bag. At dinner I said, "Papa, guess who got FOUR?" and laughed. Papa looked at me, and I thought he'd say I was the good one. But he just rubbed his eyes and said, "Not now, Divyansh."
Later I told Mummy that Mohit hid the test. I thought she would be pleased with me. She just sighed.
Mohit didn't talk to me all evening. When I went to sleep he had turned his back. He whispered, "I'll never tell you anything again."
I thought I'd feel like the winner. I don't.
Divyansh

qa.q: What did Mohit get in his spelling test?
What did Divyansh want when telling on Mohit?
qa.a: Divyansh wanted Papa and Mummy to see Divyansh as the good one and be pleased.

qa.q: What could Divyansh do next time he finds out about Mohit's mistake?
qa.a: He could keep it private or even offer to help with spelling, instead of mocking or reporting, so Mohit can trust Divyansh again.

qa.q: How does Mohit feel after the dinner?
qa.a: He feels hurt and betrayed, which is why he turned his back and said he'd never tell Divyansh anything again.

grounding: It shows a child mocking a brother's failure and telling on him to win a parent's approval, leaving a tired parent and a brother with a real grievance.

passage: Evening in the village, and Sharmila had just come back from the fields, her feet dusty and her back aching. Before she could sit, Minakshi ran up. "Amma! Madhu broke the pot at the well and he fell in the mud, he looked so silly!" She laughed and flapped her arms like him falling. "And he didn't do his homework!" Madhu stood behind the door, his face red. Sharmila closed her eyes. "Minakshi, enough." Minakshi's smile faded. She had expected Amma to say, good girl for telling. Madhu glared at her and went to the back of the house. He didn't call her for their usual game of stones that night.

qa.q: What did Minakshi say Madhu broke?
qa.a: She said he broke the pot at the well.

qa.q: What did Minakshi expect when she told Amma?
qa.a: She hoped Amma would praise her as a good girl for telling, so she felt let down when Amma said 'enough' and her smile faded.

qa.q: What went wrong, and what could fix it?
qa.a: Mocking and reporting Madhu only tired Amma and hurt Madhu; Minakshi could say sorry to Madhu, and Amma could later talk to each child calmly and separately.

qa.q: How does Madhu feel after being mocked in front of Amma?
qa.a: He feels humiliated and angry, so he glares at his sister and skips their usual game of stones.

grounding: It illustrates a child mocking her brother and telling on him to gain adult favour, which only wearies the parent and gives the brother a real grievance.
